1. A neutral verifier (not a consensus participant, no full tree) can verify inclusion proofs of state items against a published root.
2. The proof is compact (verkle-style vector commitments give O(log n) small proofs vs merkle O(log n) hashes but with sibling hashes; verkle proofs are ~32 bytes per key amortized via IPA/multiproofs).
3. Determinism: two independent implementations, given the same start (genesis + same input sequence), produce byte-identical roots.
